rationale: The foundational cohort described by Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) and indexed under OMIM entry #620938 encompasses 19 affected individuals across 10 families harboring biallelic NFU1 missense variants. Within this specific cohort, exactly 16 of 19 (84.2%) presented with early-onset pure-to-complex hereditary spastic paraplegia phenotypes with longer survival, whereas the remaining 3 of 19 (15.8%) exhibited severe infantile hypotonia and neurodevelopmental delay representing the severe end of the NFU1 continuum without the typical SPG phenotype. Literature review reveals no contradicting counts for this primary delineated cohort.

evidence.text: Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) established that across 19 affected individuals from 10 independent families with biallelic NFU1 missense variants, 16 of 19 exhibited an early-onset pure to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia phenotype with prolonged survival, whereas 3 of 19 presented with severe hypotonia and neurodevelopmental delay.

source.quote: We report 19 affected individuals from 10 independent families with ultra-rare bi-allelic NFU1 missense variants associated with a spectrum of early-onset pure to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) phenotype with a longer survival (16/19) on one end and neurodevelopmental delay with severe hypotonia (3/19) on the other.

new_directions.question_text: What specific biochemical and functional threshold differentiates NFU1 missense variants that result in MMDS1 versus SPG93 spastic paraplegia?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying how residual iron-sulfur cluster scaffold activity dictates whether an infant develops lethal pulmonary hypertension/lactic acidosis versus a prolonged-survival spastic paraplegia could predict clinical course at birth.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence of transient or remitting febrile decompensations in SPG93 versus non-mitochondrial forms of hereditary spastic paraplegia?
new_directions.rationale: Kaiyrzhanov et al. and Tonduti et al. noted relapsing-remitting deterioration and post-febrile decompensations in NFU1 patients, which may serve as the primary discriminating clinical feature distinguishing SPG93 from common HSP mimics like SPG4 or SPG7.
